newsitem.title: UK: CE Electric criticises Northern bid defence.
newsitem.headline: CE Electric criticises Northern bid defence.

text.p: CE Electric from the U.S. criticised takeover target Northern Electric Plc for using inconsistent and misleading comparisons to suggest the American firm's bid of 650 per share bid is too low.

"The board of Northern Electric and its advisers continue to use a misleading and incorrect comparison of the East Midlands offer to support a value for Northern Electric," CE Electric said. U.S. Energy group Dominion Resources has offered 670 pence per share for East Midlands Electricity Plc.
"Our final offers clearly represent full value," CE Electric's chairman and chief executive David Sokol said in a statement.
A proper comparison between Northern and Midlands would suggest a price of 603 and 645 pence per Northern share, CE Electric said.
CE Electric said that Northern's comparison failed to take into account that Midlands is facing an agreed bid and the difference in accounting principles between both bid targets.
It noted that Northern's results "were purposely constructed during its bid defenece", while "there is now no incentive for East Midlands to flatter its results when they are published."
"Using published actual cash flows, prepared before either comoany was involved in a bid situation, gives a more genuine basis for comparing multiples," CE Electric said.
The company's offer for Nothern Eletric is open until Friday.
